findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with `===`, condition is always false
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the check `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two freshly-created Dayjs object instances with strict equality. Dayjs objects are never `===` equal to each other even when they represent the same instant, so this branch can never evaluate to true. This branch appears intended to detect a zero-length date override (start == end), which should make the whole day unavailable for the fixed host; because the comparison is dead code, such overrides silently fall through to the subsequent `isBefore`/`isSame`/`isAfter` checks instead, which may not correctly block all slots for that day, risking round-robin/fixed-host bookings being allowed when the host should be fully unavailable.

findings.title: Working-hours bound check computes `end` from the slot start time, not the slot end time
findings.body: In the new working-hours validation inside `checkIfIsAvailable`, both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`), so `start` and `end` are always identical. The intent is clearly to check that the slot's end (accounting for event length) does not exceed `workingHour.endTime`, but since `end` is actually just the slot start again, the check degenerates to only validating the start time twice. As a result, a slot that starts inside working hours but would run past the organizer's working-hours end (e.g. due to event length) is not correctly flagged as out-of-bounds by this check.

findings.title: Date parsed via `.toString()` before dayjs parsing is dependent on server local timezone
findings.body: `organizerUtcOffset` and `inviteeUtcOffset` are computed as `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(...).utcOffset()`. Calling `.toString()` on a JS `Date` renders it using the running process's local timezone (influenced by `process.env.TZ`), and that string is then re-parsed by dayjs. This indirection is unnecessary (dayjs can accept the `Date` object directly, e.g. `dayjs(override.start)`), and if the server process's timezone isn't fixed to UTC, this round-trip can shift the instant being parsed and produce an incorrect UTC offset for the override, undermining the very timezone fix this PR is making.

findings.title: No fallback when `override.timeZone` is undefined, unlike the equivalent code in slots.ts (trpc router)
findings.body: `TimeRange.timeZone` (packages/types/schedule.d.ts) is declared optional, yet `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` here uses it directly without any guard. If any override lacks a `timeZone` (whether from another caller of `getSlots`, or any upstream data path that doesn't populate this newly-added field), `.tz(undefined)` will silently resolve to some default/guessed timezone instead of throwing, producing a silently wrong offset. Note that the companion logic added in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts` (`organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0`) does defensively guard against a missing timezone, making this omission inconsistent and a latent correctness risk.

findings.title: No regression test added for the PR's headline fix: fixed-host date overrides in round-robin events
findings.body: The PR description states the primary fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts are now taken into account for round-robin events, preventing round-robin bookings when a fixed host is unavailable (fixes #8207/#8329/#8273). However, the only test added in this file (around line 788) covers a personal, non-team event with a date override across two timezones — it does not exercise a ROUND_ROBIN event type with a fixed host plus a round-robin host where the fixed host has a date override. The existing round-robin test at this location (line 1032) was not extended to cover date overrides either. Without such a test, the main behavioral fix claimed by the PR has no automated regression coverage.

findings.title: Date-override day matching does not account for invitee timezone, and isn't tested across larger offsets
findings.body: The `activeOverrides` filter compares `dayjs.utc(override.start)` (which encodes the organizer's local override time as raw UTC digits) against `startOfInviteeDay`/`endOf('day')` computed in the invitee's timezone, without adjusting for the difference between organizer and invitee timezones before deciding which day's override applies. The only added test uses a 30-minute timezone difference (IST vs Dhaka), which is too small to expose day-boundary issues. For larger timezone differences (e.g. organizer and invitee many hours apart), this day-matching could select the wrong day's override, or miss an override entirely, since the comparison is done before the organizer/invitee offset adjustment is applied to determine the true instant.
